name: enscape
label: Enscape

maps.notes: sRGB. Keep to 4k: Enscape is a realtime engine and the texture budget is the framerate.

Enscape's material model prefers height/bump over a normal map. Modest relief: heavy height reads as noise at realtime framerates. Bump by default; 'use as displacement' only where the host geometry supports it.
Near-zero roughness in Enscape produces smeared reflections that look like a bug, which is why this preset clamps the low end at 0.08 rather than 0.05.
Near-binary. Enscape interpolates metallic smoothly, and mid values look like wet plastic.
Not Enscape's first choice -- the height map is. Exported because every other target in a project wants it.
Enscape computes its own screen-space occlusion. Adding an AO map produces dark-in-the-wrong-places. Exported for other renderers and for masking.
Only where the material genuinely emits.

notes: Enscape: albedo -> Albedo, height -> Height, roughness -> Roughness, metallic -> Metallic. Leave every data map's colour space set to linear/non-colour. Do not add the AO map -- Enscape generates its own ambient occlusion.
Amplitude: about 2 mm for a tile, 4 mm for brick, and check it against the tile's real size.
Material packages (.matpkg) are undocumented. This export is the PNG set plus this sheet, not a .matpkg.
Enscape has no material scripting, so the handoff is a wiring sheet rather than a script.
If your project is large, render at 2048 rather than 4096: the difference is invisible at walkthrough speed and the memory is not.
